A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work despite the changed title and CTL-to-CFT renaming. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original sentiment-classification experiments, five-run F1 results, component ablations, and sensitivity analyses in Section 6 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results in Section 6 and Appendix C, describing both experimental designs as semi-synthetic.

M1.justification: The core CTL/CFT procedure matches, including representation alignment and shuffled-feature adjustment. However, v1 describes an MLP producing Φ and a separate p(Φ|x) update, whereas v2 describes embedding-layer pooling and omits that update. The PDFs do not establish whether this reflects an implementation change or a corrected description.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate sentiment classification using Amazon and Yelp reviews with stop-word and platform-marker correlations. Renaming the second experiment from real-world to semi-synthetic does not change its underlying data or test scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: SFT0 and SFT appear in Experiment 1, with SWA and WISE additionally evaluated in Experiment 2. The CTL-N, CTL-C, and CTL-Φ variants correspond to the renamed CFT variants.

E3.justification: The reported experimental settings retain 5,000 training samples and 2,000 test samples per class, 20% validation, ten epochs, AdamW learning rates, and the same spurious-correlation proportions. The newly specified feature-extraction layer is additional documentation; no previous layer setting is explicitly replaced.

E4.justification: The component ablations and analyses of spurious-pattern strength, training-data size, and inference-sample count are retained. Appendix C presents the same evidence after renumbering and resizing. The new Section 6.3 discusses experimental design without adding an analysis.

E5.justification: Both versions report five different-seed runs, the same simulator seed policy, mean scores, and boxplots. No repeated-run counts or uncertainty-reporting procedures are added or revised.

E6.justification: Tables 1–2 add explicit differences relative to SFT, such as +9.16 for Yelp and +11.44 for the mixed-source experiment at 10% spurious correlation. All 120 underlying mean-score entries and all six empirical plot images are unchanged; these annotations do not represent performance improvements between versions.

T1.justification: v2 replaces the raw-input decomposition with a representation-level definition of do(x), formalizes shift, confounding, and invertibility requirements, and adds a maximum-entropy default-regime argument. Appendix D substantively revises the earlier Theorem 2 proof using representation interventions and a back-door step, although the final adjustment formula remains unchanged.

C1.justification: The central single-domain causal fine-tuning contribution remains. v2 narrows the empirical claim from semi-synthetic plus real-world validation to semi-synthetic evidence and replaces the emphasis on mild assumptions with explicit model-dependent identification. It also presents language models as a case study within a broader foundation-model framing.

C2.justification: v2 substantially expands the justification for choosing the interventional predictor, discussing maximum-entropy defaults, limitations of minimax alternatives, and when marginalizing confounders may help. New Section 6.3 defends controlled semi-synthetic evaluation. The conclusion also redirects future applicability from language generation toward multimodal confounding.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies embedding-layer extraction with k=1, explicitly explains discarding the frozen model after training, and expands algorithm explanations in Appendix E. v1's future code-release promise is replaced by a reference to corresponding code without a project access link.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion is substantially repositioned around transportability, confounded shifts, causal representations, and compositional interventions. Added references include Dawid, Pearl and Bareinboim, and Alabdulmohsin et al.; numerous earlier architecture and adversarial-fine-tuning references are removed. This exceeds citation-style or bibliographic changes.

P1.justification: The abstract, opening section, related work, preliminaries, and method exposition are extensively rewritten. CTL becomes CFT, the title and author block change, the motivating case study moves to Appendix A.3, and the proof and algorithms are reorganized into Appendices D and E.

P2.justification: v2 splits and redraws the original causal illustration, adds the workflow diagram in Figure 3, and redesigns Tables 1–2 with grouped headers, shading, and difference annotations. Algorithm boxes and empirical plots are relocated or resized; the additional figure numbering does not indicate new empirical plots.

improvement.justification: v2 more accurately characterizes its empirical evidence as semi-synthetic and makes the causal assumptions, derivation, and training pipeline easier to inspect through Sections 3–5 and Appendices D–E. These improve transparency. Ambiguous revised loss and local-feature notation, together with unresolved citations in Section 5, limit the overall gain.
